title: Feedback on this cutscene?
author: aj_marshall
selftext:
Hi all,

  
I made this prototype scene using Fable 5m2 and three.js 

​​I've always loved the idea of incredulously large monsters, and the game I am working on plops you in a world where your solar system is patrolled by Tianlong, a benelovent(?) dragon god(?). The game involves you discovering the origins of Tianlong to determine if he is friend or foe, and take action to leave the solar system to his whims or dare to try and save your world from him. 

  
I understand there is some minor clipping and modeling issues in this scene, but what else sticks out to you? Do you find this scene compelling, or interesting? 

  
Thanks

comments.author: Particular_Park_391
comments.body: That was incredible! I liked how the dragon was way bigger than expected. Would be cool if it caused a tsunami or something too.

comments.author: mars_santa
comments.body:
I really like creatures at that scale, I don't see nearly enough of them in games. Very convincing effect but it does look like the horizon cuts off when it would be rounded more I think. 

Great work!

comments.author: DerrickBarra
comments.body: I like the background, looks peaceful. Until the dragon shows up.

comments.author: BrotherMoy
comments.body: I'll give some criticism since it seems nobody else. The background and environment looks like a photorealistic cubemap, it would be cooler if it looked like the dragon (same art style). The cutscene is way too slow, if you're forced to actually watch this, it's way too slow. However if you can move around while this is is going on and look anywhere then it's fine. The sound doesn't match the epicness of the dragon flying in, there probably needs to be low grumbling, along with the wind sounds you have. The environment should also do things to match the dragon like dirt or smoke flying everywhere (tsunami like someone else said). Honestly pretty epic large flying creature though, I think you gotta build everything else around it

comments.author: stoneofthewise
comments.body: Are you controlling the camera with your mouse during this cut scene because it looks like it. If not, the camera movement should be smoother. The lighting environment and the dragon are pretty incredible though I feel like the dragon head could possibly have a little bit more motion to it, especially when it’s nearest to the camera.

replies.author: rhjads
replies.body:
yeah this was my feeling as well, the movement is choppy. Also if i'm not controlling the view/camera during the scene i find it quite long before something happens.   
Like how it looks. The sound is something that good add to it, i feel this isnt at the level of the graphics yet

comments.author: Famous_Ad_5611
comments.body:
The idea is awsome and execution (considering the thread) is absolutly nice; Good job, you subverted my excpectations - thats a nice feeling. 

If I had to cricitise - it's to long. cut like 25% of it - it's currently 2 minutes, it should be max 1:30 ;p

comments.author: Kurk_Lazaris
comments.body: It's good! A music would add to the cataclysmic element.

comments.author: AdStreet4350
comments.body: Really cool but yeah the art style of the dragon are pretty weird
